_what: The one home this engine keeps on a computer, and the one list of what may sit at its top (src/native_entry/home.rs). The home is `default` (under the person's home folder) unless the one launch setting `setting` names another absolute folder; nothing else moves it. `entries` has one row per allowed top-level entry: its name, whether it is a folder or a file, its job in one plain sentence, who writes it (the engine, the app, a Workshop tool, an AI command-line hook, the person, or nobody: no writer found in any repository, listed because today's home holds it) and where that writer is (`source`, a repository and file:line, found by grep on 2026-11-04). An engine row names the engine DATA file that reads it (`reader`): an engine path is a home entry and a path inside it, and the engine refuses an entry that is not an engine row here before it makes anything. `undeclared_entries` lists what sits in a home without a row. A row with `moved_from` is a job folder not in the home yet: its data still sits where `moved_from` says, and `moves` lists each such entry and its job folder. Data moves only after its reader is changed and released (reader change, then move); this file moves nothing. Names are by job, with no dates, codes or hashes (a file's name may end in lowercase extensions such as `.json` or `.sealed.log`); renaming a folder a running program reads needs that program's release, so a rename is its own change.
